about: What the command-bookkeeping simulator adds to a fault profile (faults/<name>.json gives the per-transaction crash_before_commit, crash_after_commit and interrupt_mid_statement chances, applied to every transaction of the book, the gate and the quota owner). Idle eviction is platform physics and runs in every profile: a Durable Object with no request, alarm or pending timer is evicted after 70-140 s of inactivity, and a pending setTimeout keeps it in memory (Cloudflare Durable Objects lifecycle, developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/concepts/durable-object-lifecycle, read 2026-10-28). A restart is a deploy or host move: every object loses its memory at once, whatever it held. A policy update fences the gate, drains what is in flight, and changes one thing: it ends the person's sign-in for revoke_minutes (a later update restores it), lowers or raises the paid ceiling, or changes nothing else. A client stall holds one step of a command before it is sent (a slow worker, a request queued behind others); a stall longer than the idle window lets the book be evicted between two steps of one command.
